newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower after SMI sets record high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower after SMI sets record high.

text.p: Swiss shares ended lower on Wednesday after profit-taking undermined gains which took the Swiss Market Index (SMI) to new record highs in early trade.
Heavyweights Novartis and Nestle led the market down.
Sentiment remained favourable, however, dealers said.

Further developments would likely depend on how the market reacts to Roche's 1996 sales figures which are due ahead of the bourse opening on Thursday. Roche participation certificates added 110 francs to 10,850.

The blue-chip SMI ended down 4.0 points, or 0.1 percent, at 3,979.67 after hitting an all-time high of 4,004.8 points in early trade. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) fell 3.66 points, or 0.14 percent, to 2,551.75.
Industrials including SMH and Sulzer posted advances of more than one percent amid good demand for cyclicals.
Banks fell on concerns about negative publicity over their dispute with Jewish groups concerning dormant accounts of Holocaust victims.

UBS bearer shares slid 0.87 percent or 10.00 francs to 1,146 francs. SBC fell two percent, or 5.00 francs, to 245.50 francs. SMH bearer shares jumped 1.27 percent or 11 francs to 874. Sulzer soared more than two percent, or 17 francs, to 854. ABB ended up 13 francs at 1,671. Alusuisse was battered by a downgrade of CSFB, giving up nine francs to end at 1,109.
Swissair gave up 23 francs to end at 1,115.
